subject: Control plane: SCIM de-dup behavior & delegated-admin mapping
messages:

Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SCIM provisioning creating duplicate operator accounts after SAML SSO rollout

Hi Stephanie,

We rolled the SAML SSO change live this morning and observed that several operator accounts in the private control plane were duplicated after SCIM provisioning ran. Example: user alice@helmtech created two operator entries (alice and alice+1) with different role sets.

Attached is a short provisioning log showing the SCIM POST responses for the affected users and the SAML assertion IDs from this morning's sign-ins. Can you help us understand whether Redwood's SCIM adapter can dedupe based on externalId or if there's an expected mapping we missed?

High level ask: we need a safe rollback or reconciliation approach that won't remove legitimate JIT-created operator entitlements. HelmTech is paused on ramping this customer-facing workload until this is resolved.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Re: SCIM provisioning creating duplicate operator accounts after SAML SSO rollout

Elena — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. I'm looping in Kim and Ben from Identity/Provisioning.

Initial read: duplicates often happen when Redwood's SCIM provisioning sees two distinct external identifiers (externalId or id attribute) on the same email, or when downstream provisioning retries create a new principal instead of updating. We need to confirm:

- Which attribute does HelmTech populate as the SCIM externalId? (email, employeeId, or the SAML NameID?)
- Were there simultaneous provisioning events (you mentioned SSO rollout time) — any bursts shown in your logs?

Immediate mitigation options we can propose:
1) Pause SCIM outbound for the "operator" group while we reconcile (safe but pauses new provisioning).
2) Apply an idempotency/lookup patch to the SCIM adapter to prefer externalId over matching by email.
3) Run a one-off reconciliation that creates mapping rows for the duplicate principals and consolidates entitlements (non-destructive merge).

I'll get Ben to confirm the adapter behavior and Kim to surface the simplest reconciliation script. Can HelmTech share the role-mapping CSV? the one you sent looked truncated.

- Stephanie

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@helmtech.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SCIM provisioning creating duplicate operator accounts after SAML SSO rollout

Stephanie / Kim / Elena — digging into the adapter code and today's provisioning trace. A few notes: 

1) Current behavior: the private control plane SCIM integrator attempts to match incoming SCIM users by externalId first (if present), then by email. However, during SSO cutovers we occasionally receive SAML assertions where the NameID (which HelmTech currently maps to user.id and also to externalId) transiently changes (e.g., when you swap federated IdP connectors). If externalId changes, the adapter creates a new principal.

2) Retried provisioning (retries from HelmTech on 500s) are logged as new POST attempts. We only de-duplicate when externalId matches exactly. No fuzzy merges.

3) Reconciliation path: safest is a non-destructive mapping table that links oldPrincipalId -> canonicalPrincipalId and a permission-copy job that runs during a maintenance window. We can ship a small script (Python) that:
   - queries both principals
   - writes a merge plan (CSV)
   - applies role grants to canonical principal
   - disables the duplicate principal with a tombstone flag (keeps history)

4) Quick fix: if HelmTech can ensure SCIM externalId uses a stable helmtech:userId (not NameID), and the SSO config maps NameID only for assertion, we avoid the churn.

I'm attaching a diff of our role mapping heuristics for review (see role-mapping-diff.csv).

Proposed next steps:
- HelmTech: confirm externalId attribute value and share full provisioning dump for the window 07:50–09:30 PT.
- Redwood: prepare reconciliation script + docs; propose maintenance window tonight 22:00–23:00 PT for non-destructive merge.

Ben
Engineering Manager, Identity Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: HelmTech SRE <sre@helmtech.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SCIM provisioning creating duplicate operator accounts after SAML SSO rollout

Thanks for the quick analysis. Confirming: HelmTech used NameID (transient connector ID) as externalId during the initial SSO cutover — that was our mistake. We've attached the full provisioning dump (split) and the SAML assertion IDs for the same window. We can target the 22:00 maintenance window but would like the reconciliation to be reversible.

A couple of constraints to call out so reconciliation doesn't break supportability: 
- Do not delete any principal rows; prefer tombstone and metadata copy.
- Keep an audit column linking back to the original SAML assertion IDs.
- We need to coordinate rollback steps in case downstream access logs show anomalies.

We'll also patch the SCIM payload to populate externalId with helmtech:employeeId going forward.

— HelmTech SRE

Subject: Re: SCIM provisioning creating duplicate operator accounts after SAML SSO rollout

Summary and action items (agreed):

1) HelmTech will update SCIM to set externalId=helmtech:employeeId for all operator users (non-transient) — target: 2025-10-22 06:00 UTC.
2) Redwood will deliver a reconciliation script by 20:00 PT today and run it in a supervised maintenance window 22:00–23:00 PT. Script behavior: non-destructive merge (copy roles, add tombstone flag, write audit mapping to SUP-4321).
3) Redwood to add an adapter safeguard that logs when externalId changes between consecutive provisioning events for the same email (we'll roll this as a hotfix to the adapter).
4) If any anomalies appear post-merge, rollback path: re-enable duplicated principal and restore role mappings from the tombstone snapshot — both steps are recorded in the runbook.

Jordan, can you confirm the runbook entries and that the fix will not affect dedicated-instance tenancy constraints?

Thanks everyone — I'll open SUP-4321 and attach the scripts/outputs.

-Stephanie
